subject.title: Background PTY exec runs can survive restart/session loss and become untracked orphan process trees

question: For OpenClaw-owned background PTY exec runs that survive gateway restart or session-state loss, should startup reconciliation kill stale process trees, re-register recoverable runs, or limit the fix to live in-process drift?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent behavior affects operator expectations, session-state recovery, process ownership, and the security/availability boundary for killing live descendants after restart.

options.title: Kill stale OpenClaw-owned runs on startup
options.body: Persist enough ownership metadata to identify prior-epoch OpenClaw exec trees and terminate them conservatively during gateway startup or doctor repair.

options.title: Re-register recoverable runs
options.body: Attempt to restore tracked sessions for live prior-epoch PTY runs, accepting a more complex state and identity contract to preserve work.

options.title: Only fix in-process drift
options.body: Adopt the narrower linked-PR approach for same-process registry drift and leave cold-start orphan reaping to a separate design.

recommendation.title: Kill stale OpenClaw-owned runs on startup
recommendation.body: Persist enough ownership metadata to identify prior-epoch OpenClaw exec trees and terminate them conservatively during gateway startup or doctor repair.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history across the inspected supervisor, process-tool, and session-adjacent surfaces.
